description: This plot illustrates the relationship between "Initial Confidence" and "Accuracy" across three different metrics: Final Accuracy, $\Delta$ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy. The x-axis represents "Initial Confidence" on a linear scale ranging from 0.86 to 1.00, with tick marks placed at 0.86, 0.88, and subsequently at intervals of 0.01 up to 1.00. The y-axis represents "Accuracy" on a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick labels spaced at intervals of 0.2. The plot contains three lines, all of which feature vertical error bars at each data point. The "Final Accuracy" is depicted by a solid blue line with circle markers; it begins at a value of approximately 0.93 at x=0.86, remains relatively steady with a slight peak near 1.00 at x=0.97, and ends at approximately 0.98 at x=1.00. The "$\Delta$ Accuracy" is shown as a dashed brown line with diamond markers; it starts at approximately 0.28 at x=0.86, exhibits a general downward trend to a low of roughly 0.05 at x=0.95, and then rises to end at approximately 0.21 at x=1.00. The "Initial Accuracy" is represented by a dash-dot green line with square markers; it starts at approximately 0.64 at x=0.86, generally increases to reach peaks of approximately 0.93 at x=0.95 and x=0.99, before declining to end at approximately 0.77 at x=1.00.
